transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess... something happened at work. We had a staff meeting and... I don't know, I just got kind of worked up. I started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill right there in the room. Just... moving chairs around, waving my arms. Folks kept telling me to sit down, but... I couldn't seem to stop. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
What was going through your mind at that moment that made you feel you had to do that drill?

I just... I don't know. I guess I felt like I had to prove I knew what I was doing. Even when I'm not acting like that, when I'm just doing my job... I know my supervisor and a few of the others are watching me. They keep notes. They make these little comments to test me. It's like they're trying to build a case that I'm not safe around the seniors. So... I just had to show them I knew the drill.
Over the past several days or weeks, have you found yourself needing much less sleep than usual while still feeling energetic?

Um... yeah, I guess. I've been sleeping maybe two, three hours a night. I wake up way before the sun's even up, and... I just feel fine. Ready to go. I just sit there in the dark, figuring things out, making plans. It doesn't really seem like a problem to me.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt very down, depressed, or lost interest in things for a couple of weeks or more?
Um... no. Not really. I mean, everybody gets a little down sometimes, but... nothing like that. I just... I go to work, I do my job. That's it.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?

I mean... sometimes. Just... if I'm by myself. Like, if I'm in the hallway at work, or... down by the laundry room at my place. I'll hear someone say my name, or... I'll hear one of the seniors calling out for help. It sounds real. Clear as day. But... I go look, and there's nobody around.
Have you ever heard those voices or felt people were watching you during times when your sleep and energy were completely normal?

I mean... yeah. I guess. There was a stretch where things were... calmer. I was actually sleeping okay, not really rushing around doing all those projects. 

But... even then, for a few weeks, I'd still hear it. My name. And... I don't know, I just... I was still pretty sure people at work were keeping notes on me. So... yeah.
Looking back over the entire time you have had these experiences, have these periods of high energy and needing less sleep been present for most of that time, or only a small part of it?

I guess... most of it. If I look back... those times where I'm all wired up, you know, making big plans and... having a short fuse... that's taken up a lot more of the time than the calmer weeks. So... yeah. Mostly that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for schizoaffective disorder, manic type (F25.0). There is clear concurrent presentation of manic symptoms (markedly decreased need for sleep, excessive energy, psychomotor agitation, grandiose/pressured behaviors) and psychotic symptoms (persecutory delusions regarding coworkers keeping notes and auditory hallucinations of voices calling their name/asking for help). Crucially, the patient endorsed a distinct period of at least two weeks of psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and paranoid delusions) in the absence of prominent mood disturbance, distinguishing schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
